title: CASE OF A. v. THE NETHERLANDS
conclusion: Violation of Art. 3 (in case of expulsion to Libya);No violation of Art. 13;Pecuniary damage - claim dismissed;Non-pecuniary damage - finding of violation sufficient
summary: In the case of A. v. the Netherlands, the applicant, a Libyan national of Roma and Traveller identity, challenged the Dutch authorities’ decision to expel him to Libya. The case focused on the vulnerability of Roma and Travellers facing persecution and ill-treatment upon return to their country of origin. The applicant had fled Libya in 1994 due to his involvement with an opposition group opposing the Libyan regime, fearing arrest and persecution. After a complex journey through several countries, he sought asylum in the Netherlands in 1997. Despite his claims and supporting statements from a Libyan opposition organisation, Dutch authorities rejected his asylum request, doubting the credibility of his involvement and the risk he faced. The applicant contested the decision, arguing that expulsion to Libya would expose him to treatment violating Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which prohibits torture and inhuman or degrading treatment. The European Court of Human Rights examined Articles 3 and 13 and found a violation of Article 3 concerning the risk of expulsion to Libya, while no violation of Article 13 was established. The Court did not award pecuniary damages but considered the finding of a violation sufficient for non-pecuniary damage. This judgment is significant as it reaffirms the protection against forced return to countries where Roma and Travellers face serious human rights abuses, reflecting ongoing challenges for these minorities in securing asylum and protection in Europe.
